patterns.content: Prefer const over let; never var. const does not mean immutable — object properties can still change. Use Object.freeze() for true immutability.
Destructuring: const { name, age = 0 } = user; const [first, ...rest] = items; function f({ id, label }) — avoids repeated property access.
async/await over raw Promises. try/catch for error handling. Promise.all([p1, p2]) for parallel. Promise.allSettled() when partial failure is acceptable.
Optional chaining and nullish coalescing: user?.address?.city ?? 'Unknown'. Avoids null-check chains.
Array methods over loops: .map(), .filter(), .reduce(), .find(), .some(), .every(). Chaining is idiomatic; avoid mutations inside map/filter.
Spread and rest: const merged = { ...defaults, ...overrides }; const copy = [...arr]; function f(...args) — avoids Object.assign and .apply().
Modules: use import/export (ESM) not require/module.exports (CJS) for new code. Use dynamic import() for lazy loading.
Template literals for string interpolation: `Hello ${name}, you have ${count} messages.` — also for multiline strings.
Error handling: always propagate or log errors. Never empty catch. throw new Error('message') not throw 'message' (string throws lose stack traces).
WeakMap/WeakRef for object metadata that should not prevent GC. Map for ordered key-value pairs. Set for unique values. Prefer these over plain objects where appropriate.
